comment: Looked clean and tidy, good breakfast selection. Slightly concerned about lower rating but still closer to city center than higher rated options and I`d be concerned about transportation into the conference centre, plus from pictures it did look very clean so doubt low rating would be over that. Since it is for a short stay I chose conveniance of being closer to city center rather than higher rating.

Seemed the neatest and cleanest which is most important for me, and seemed to be the most modern as well. Slightly farther away from city centre but still within 1 mile and I am aware Paris has good public transportation so would not be too worried. Good customer rating as well. Other hotels seemed like they would make me uncomfortable from pictures despite some having higher ratings so this was the obvious choice for me.

Despite room seeming to be quite dark and the overall ambiance of the hotel not being my style and what I would normally choose, it did look clean and modern. Most important area for me in this one was closeness to city centre as I do not know Amsterdam and would not be comfortable being far away. The pictures looked nice and the rating was good so confident it would be a pleasant hotel.

Again as I am unfamiliar with the city I would prefer to be close to the city centre, and out of the two choices that were closest this one had a bathroom that looked more up to date and to my liking, and had a considerably higher overall rating. I would have gone with the other more highly rated hotels as they looked more modern and attractive but the distance would have concerned me.
This was in the middle in terms of closeness to the city centre, but had a very high rating and looked like the sleekest and most modern option.
Selection was made based on its proximity to the city center. It also didn't have bad ratings

7 feels by comparison very respectable but its closeness undeniably makes it an attractive option

The hotel has good reviews and is not too far from the city. The closer options did not have as good reviews or look as nice as my chosen accommodation. Having the ability to stay in a nice comfortable hotel but without compromising my ability to get to and from the city center was important. While other options were closer, I did not want to risk bad service or accommodation experience just for convience. The other hotel with higher ratings was too far to justify the difference in rating.

The hotel has almost the best ratings, and while it is farther from the city centre, it should not be hard to navigate the city since Barcelona has a good functioning public transport system. Other options were closer to the city centre, but I wouldn't have chosen them based on reviews even though the pictures of the interior and exterior looked nice.

Most of the options had relatively similar ratings; however, quite a few of them are very far from the city centre. Of the two options that weren't 2.6 miles away, I chose the one with the better ratings since they were the same distance and looked relatively similar on the inside.

This hotel is a bit further outside the city compared to the other options; however, the others had much lower ratings. 1.4 miles is not too far in reality and could be traversed easily by taxi or public transport; moreover, as an employee, there would most likely be less concern to go out in the city at night and focus more on the accommodation since a lot of work and traveling could be conducted in such a short trip.

This hotel was very close to the city centre, and compared to other options with higher ratings, it did not seem like the pictures showed a significant quality difference to justify staying much further away from the city. The chosen option didn't have that low of a score, and the option that was most competitive, was more than 1.5 miles away from the city and had a review that was a little over 1 point greater than the chosen option. The difference in distance could not be justified therefore.
not far from city centre at the over average rating.
The second higest rating hotel, but it is the cloest one to the city centre. And the room seems neat and airy.

The hotel looked nice inside - not too posh and flashy. The food available looked fresh and the views from the hotel also looked appealing. The walk to the city centre was also not too far. I wouldn't like to choose a hotel that was in the centre of the city centre as it is likely to be more noisy and overpriced.
Nice distance from the city - Interior looked fairly simple and food looked good. Also happened to be the one with the highest customer rating so reaffirmed my choice.
Food looked very fresh and appetising, nice distance from the city centre - room looked decent and also had a good customer rating.
Food looked good and not loads of meat like some of the others. Again nice distance from the city centre to walk in and had a great customer rating.

It was a toss up between the two best rated hotels. However I chose this one because the food looked really good, still within walking distance of the city centre, room was more simple than the other hotel which just looked a bit too luxurious and expensive. Also happened to have the best customer rating too but was not this really veered me towards my choice.

This hotel was the closest to the city centre and had a really good rating. The room looked very satisfcatory for a 3 night trip. While there were 2 hotels with slightly nicer looking rooms, they were located 2.6 miles away from the city centre and would require additional travel costs to get into the city centre (something which I'd have to take into account as a postgrad student)
This hotel was the closest to the city centre. Despite having the lowest user rating, I personally thought the room looked satisfactory.
It is a satisfactory hotel that is relatively close to the city centre. It also has a lovely balcony view of the city (which is an added bonus).
Hotel is close to the city centre and the room looks nice.
close to the city centre and the room looks nice. It also has a decent user rating.

When comparing the distance to the city centre and the average customer rating, it gave me the best possible experience being convient and comfort in relation to the average rating. The photos also looked appealing, ensuring my decision to go with this hotel.

It offered me the nicest accomodation within a reasonable distance to the city centre, based on the customer average rating. Also, looking at the pictures I appealed to me a lot more when compared to the other hotels within the same distance to the city centre.

The hotel judging from the images and the average customer rating is worth the extra distance when compared to the other hotel options. Considering the accomodation is covered by an external source rather than myself, I feel as if I would take advantage of this opportunity and stay in somewhere that would normally be out of my price range. The distance to city centre is also short enough that I would not have to leave a considerable amount of time for a commute to the conference.

I chose this hotel because in the images it looked the nicest as well as the having the highest average customer rating. Despite it being the furthest away, the distance was not considerable enough to put me off due to the fact that it was much more appealing than the other hotels.

This hotel appealed to me the most despite the average customer rating. The closeness to the city centre also played a contributing factor in my decision making when compared to the rest of the hotels.
Because distance is the first priority criteria while I choose hotel then rating goes after
this hotel has high rating with acceptable distance that i'm interested in.
I would like to choose the hotel which rate is over 8 because I think  the hotels having over 8 are not so different. Thus, next driver to choose is distance.

Still, I think the rating is the important figure that I need to consider. However, as a PG student attending the conference in Athenes, I also would like to travel and explore the city. Therefore, the distance to city centre became more important than how comfortable and how quiet the place is. The place is second nearest to the city centre as well as slightly higher rating compared to the nearest one. In other words, the proximity to the city centre and the rating has been considered.

As I am going to Frankfurt for the training, I would be definitely exhausted by the time it ends. Thus, rating again is the most important figure in terms of meals, coziness and kindness. Although the hotel I chose is the farthest from the city centre, it wouldn't affect my decision that much since I am not going there for sightseeing or enjoying the vacation. If I really want to drink and have some kind of party, I may as well use Uber or Taxi and come back to the residence. So, the rating is by far the most important thing to see as always.

In this case, the city at which I am going to be seems also important. If I were any other scenarios such as going Athenes or Frankfurt, I would have chosen the one with the highest rank. Yet in this case, I considered both location and the atmostphere of the accommodation. Paris is perceived to be romantic city among foreigners, which encourages people to explore and feel the city even though this is a business trip. So, I picked the one with second-highest rating while the atmostphere of the residence is exotic. Still, the proximity to the city centre is not significant information in deciding the accommodation.

In this case, it is exceptional case and I am irrational since I was aspire to go Barcelona. So, I would like to spend whole night being in the city centre while having a party and enjoy the night. Rating doesn't matter that much and the proximity in this case is the most important. (I am not sure this explanation makes sense to the experiment to be honest :( but sometimes people become irrational in a specific situation you know, i think this is everyday life situation that we encounter)

In this case, both the proximity and the rating has been considered since there is just lilttle difference between the one with the highest ranking, yet furthest from the city centre. Therefore, the proximity was taken into account in this case.

In a city like Barcelona my upmost priority would not be the luxury of the hotel, it is such a beautiful city that is so worth exploring that I would want to be close to the centre, that being said this one looked nicer than the one that was 0.1 miles closer to the centre. the picture of the room showed that it had a nice view and the room in general had a nicer atmosphere - it also had higher ratings.

From the sounds of the brief there wouldn't be much time to experience Frankfurt so here my priority was a nice space to relax following the training, i nearly went for the one that was 0.7 miles from the centre but the pictures of the room and the waffle maker at the breakfast buffet really cinched this one for me. It just looks like a pretty damn nice hotel even if the exterior isn't the prettiest.

Despite this hotel having a slightly lower rating than the other central amsterdam hotel the colour scheme inside was soooo much nicer, much rather take black and white photography behind a headrest than an abundance of lime green. For me the only real choices were these two central hotels as in the brief it says about it being a two day affair with three nights stay paid for, this means that it would be worth being close to the centre of Amsterdam for that free day, could really take advantage of it rather than being stuck on transport to get into the centre.

it was definitely the views that where the decider for me, in a city like Athens what I'd want to see/visit isn't the centre but the beautiful historic landmarks and this hotel clearly offers this - plus it has very high ratings and looks nice

Also the centrality of its location means that if the wierd deco starts to get too much it is easy to escape onto the beautiful streets of Paris.

For myself in this situation I would look to have the nicest possible hotel, my second choice would be the 7.0 rated closer to the city, but the vast difference in rating (2.0) put me off. As someone who has booked a lot of trips in the past I know how vital a good rating is and these have been and will be always the things I look at. Ultimately less than a mile is not that much further to walk or get a taxi if the place is nice.

Second choice is defintely the hotel with views of the acropolis from the restaurant and temple of Zeus from the front, however, with no guaruntee on being able to use the restaurant in the time there and the reviews and distance being better for the chosen hotel this is sacrificed. However, with time to explore this is no great problem. More so, the rooms etc in the chosen hotel look amazing with the light and coloured walls.
Close to city center, good level of rating, nice decor and looking hotel in general, obvious choice.

The cellar restaurant was the unique selling point for me here. The decor in the higher rated hotels was not my cup of tea and therefore detracted from the ratings. The chosen hotel was positionally good and decor wise not too bad, whereas the closer to the city hotels in some part seemed cramped from the pictures of the bedroom. Moreover, the inclusion of a sesk in the room and a nice restaurant space that look conducive to work was another point that made me choose it. The close second was the one slightly lower rated but slightly closer to the city centre.

I would choose this hotel solely forthe balcony room alone, amazing layout and grand fashion to the room and the rest of the hotel looked perfectly pleasant. Minor problem as far as work space goes for the room/hotel, but with a laptop sitting on the bed would be no problem. Other hotels distance was not justified by the difference in the rooms, closer hotels in part looked dingy, and with lower ratings I would be cautious to take them up.

I chose Electra Athens mostly because of the aesthetic appeal and its also the second closest to the city. If there had been reviews, this would have helped my decision better in order for me to identify specific aspects which I would be pleased with or not about the hotel.

My initial instinct was to choose the Victoria,  because its appearance appealed to me, but then the Centrum had a good balance of all the aspects to consider, in that the distance was not too far from the city centre and the rating was also in the middle of all the others. Banks Hotel looked good despite the distance to the city centre, it could be a good opportunity to explore the city whilst heading to the conference which is held in the city. Also good to make use of reliable transportation to get to the conference
